## Install and load {#installation}

The examples use the development source in this checkout, ggplot2, and the bundled data. Install ggchord from the repository root before running them.

```{r workflow-1}
remotes::install_local(".", dependencies = NA)
library(ggchord)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Compare references and their relationships {#multi-sequence-start}

Start from the complete reference table. Each observation layer takes its own data and evaluates mappings on that table. Add another geom_seq() to draw a second backbone style on the same reference, or omit the backbone while keeping the coordinate frame.

Map ribbon fill to `pident` and add `scale_fill_pident()` for the stepped Identity (%) guide from 0 to 100.

```{r workflow-2}
refs <- seq_data_example
relationships <- ribbon_data_example

comparison <- ggchord(refs) +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(fill = pident), data = relationships) +
  scale_fill_pident() +
  geom_seq(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_seq_label() +
  scale_seq_continuous(guide = "none")

comparison + coord_chord(start_angle = 90)
```

## Change the display and keep the observations {#multi-sequence-start-collinear}

The reference layout owns display order, orientation and physical spacing. The coordinate system projects that arrangement. Use an explicit orientation to reverse a displayed reference while retaining the original biological strands.

```{r workflow-3}
order <- refs$accver
direction <- setNames(c(-1, rep(1, length(order) - 1)), order)
comparison +
  layout_sequences(order = order, orientation = direction, row_gap = 8) +
  coord_collinear()
```

## Annotate one circular map {#circular-start}

Use one reference per Circular panel. Here the gene labels follow the only gene layer, including its displayed positions. With multiple compatible annotation layers, give the intended layer an ID and use that name as `anchor_layer`. `layout_label_repel()` moves the text around its anchor. Set `leader` on the label layer to control the connecting line.

```{r workflow-4}
ref <- data.frame(accver = "map", length = 1000, topology = "circular")
features <- data.frame(
  accver = "map", start = c(50, 450), end = c(360, 740),
  strand = c("+", "-"), label = c("Feature A", "Feature B")
)

ggchord() +
  geom_seq(data = ref) +
  geom_gene(data = features, fill = "#277A73") +
  geom_feature_label(aes(label = label), label_layout = layout_label_repel()) +
  layout_sequences(angular_gap = 12) +
  coord_circular() +
  theme_ggchord_plasmid()
```

## Inspect an HSP on two source axes {#dotplot-start}

Dotplot uses query coordinates for x and subject coordinates for y. Provide reliable strand evidence or an explicit relative direction. Selection and order on each axis are declared in layout_dotplot().

```{r workflow-5}
refs_pair <- data.frame(accver = c("A", "B"), length = c(1000, 800))
hsp <- data.frame(
  qaccver = "A", qstart = 120, qend = 410, qstrand = "+",
  saccver = "B", sstart = 80, send = 370, sstrand = "-"
)

ggchord(refs_pair) +
  geom_alignment_segment(data = hsp) +
  layout_dotplot(x_order = "A", y_order = "B") +
  coord_dotplot()
```

## Add a track height scale {#track-start}

A band declares physical space. The scale maps measurements to that band's height. Position is measured in the reference unit and the track's value remains in its measurement unit.

```{r workflow-6}
ref <- data.frame(accver = "A", length = 1000)
signal <- data.frame(accver = "A", pos = c(50, 250, 450, 650, 850),
  value = c(3, 7, 6, 10, 4))

ggchord(ref) +
  geom_seq() +
  layout_track("signal", thickness = 6) +
  geom_track_line(data = signal, track = "signal", colour = "#277A73") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Signal") +
  coord_collinear()
```

## Combine views of a source interval {#fusion-start}

Fusion arranges independent plots by name. A zoom layer marks that two panels display the same source interval. Use fusion_ribbon() to show an observed relationship with explicit source endpoints.

```{r workflow-7}
ref <- data.frame(accver = "A", length = 1000)
region <- data.frame(accver = "A", start = 200, end = 500)

overview <- ggchord(ref) + geom_seq() + coord_circular()
detail <- ggchord(ref) + geom_seq() +
  layout_sequences(windows = transform(region, instance_id = "detail")) +
  coord_collinear()

combined <- ggchord_fusion(list(overview = overview, detail = detail)) +
  fusion_zoom("overview", "detail", region)
combined
```

## Inspect, preview and save {#output}

Export the source stage to look up the observations contributing to a plot. Specify an output size and device when querying measured geometry. Use the same dimensions for a sized preview and the saved result.

```{r workflow-8}
export_ggchord_layout(overview, stages = "source")
view_ggchord(combined, width = 9, height = 5)
ggsave("comparison.png", combined, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 144)
```
